Think of it like your waste water. Little spurts and streams are expected as normal use. Flush a toilet, surge. Run the sink. Trickle. Sending live audio would be a trickle. You should only see a trickle when you are using the device. If it is accumulating stored audio (and memory chips would be apparent on the circuitry), it is filling up a bath tub. Your options for getting that water out are to either dump it through all at once and hope no one notices, send it in a constant trickle (which would be about as apparent as the live data trickle) or try to send it in short bursts which would also be apparent.

These are things you can do just with a bandwidth monitor. Packet inspection gets you even more information.
